As far as superheroes go, he's a human. Batman is a heavily trained human with massive amounts of money to be sure, but just a human nonetheless. As such he can come off as more relatable than those superheroes with fundementally inhuman potential. You could theoretically do the things Batman can do if given the time and money, as even if it is highly unrealistic. On the other hand, you can never shoot lasers from your eyes and fly freely like Superman. Batman is, essentially, human potential and the ability for one person to make a difference which can make him a very relatable character.

Of course, a well-written protagonist can be relatable to just about anyone as well. If you watch, say, Fox and the Hound you can generally relate to the protagonists easily despite not being even the same species. A lot of relatability is just good writing and maybe some familiar events or goals. You may find Batman relatable because he is so dedicated to a cause, from his intelligence, his moral cods, his backstory as an orphan or any number of reasons... Or just because his stories are good and appeal to your personal tastes in media.

Lots of good answers here, but some things I haven't seen yet...

  1. We get to know him. Because he's the detective, we spend a lot more time watching him NOT punching things, unlike many other heroes. And every time we see him where he's not punching things, more of his personality is expressed in some way.

  2. He's a loner. Who hasn't felt like a loner at some point in their lives? That aspect of him resonates with something deeply powerful in all of us, especially in the face of so much social pressure now-a-days to always be online and connected with people.

  3. He has the best and most relatable superpower. His superpower is basically an indomitable will and ability to think ahead and plan for everything. These things would be massively beneficial across almost all areas of our lives, and we all want to be able to do that. Super strength, speed, etc., would have way more limited benefits, we can't really picture using those well.

  4. He has the most relatable goals and methods. He's driven by loss and a righteous sense of justice. We've all experienced these. Either you lost something and had a burning desire to get it back, or you saw something on the news that made you want to go out and do something about the crappy state of the world. That's all this guy does.

  5. He's morally ambiguous. Or not. People tend to either see the world in black and white, or in shades of gray. Batman appeals to both. Clearly he's a superhero that punishes well-defined criminals and thus makes the world a better place, and the former group can focus on that aspect. But to the people who see the world as more complex than that, they can also acknowledge that he operates in ways that are unseemly to law enforcement and good order, and the latter group can focus on that.
